output:
Hey Hollins Family Ties ❤️ Putting this here so y’all can stop asking Mama: yes, I’m coming to Thanksgiving! Thursday, Nov. 26, at Aunt Denise’s in Macon, eating around 3. I’m bringing mac and cheese and two sweet potato pies.

I also want to say something before we’re all in the same room again. Last Thanksgiving, a conversation about my job turned into an argument, and I helped turn it into one. I got sarcastic and personal when I could have stopped talking. That part is mine, and I’m sorry for how I spoke at Grandma’s holiday.

For the cousins who weren’t there, you don’t need a whole recap. What matters is that Grandma Pearl ended up sitting on the porch instead of enjoying her family, and I still feel bad about that. She shouldn’t have had to leave the room to get some peace.

I’m proud of the work I do, and I’m not apologizing for that. But being proud of my work doesn’t excuse taking a cheap shot at somebody I love. We can disagree without doing that, and I want to do better this year.

So I’m asking for a one-day truce on work and politics. Also, questions about “the lawsuit” really are a dead end: I can’t discuss open cases because of confidentiality. That’s not me being difficult or mysterious. I genuinely cannot talk about them.

I know there’s still love here, even when we get on each other’s nerves. I don’t want another year of everybody wondering whether I’m coming or whether dinner is going to turn into round two.

I’m coming, I’m looking forward to seeing everybody, and I want us to have a good day. Can we keep the table conversation to food, football, babies, and Tasha’s new boyfriend? Tasha, please let him know the family has questions. 😂❤️

reasons: Leaves out the point that the relative likes to poke but isn't a bad guy, and the August thumbs-up birthday text.
